notes.decision: Translated as 'that they are sins' — picking up an ongoing speech from the previous page in which the forgiving brothers acknowledge the catechumen's wrongs as 'sins' that are now forgiven, set against the mercies they continue to show.

ⲥⲉⲃⲓ ⲛⲉⲙⲉⲕ literally 'they bear with you'; ⲍⲱⲥ ϣⲃⲏⲣ 'as a companion' — the brothers carry the catechumen as fellow-traveler. Preserves the Coptic 'bear (along) with' rather than smoothing to 'they treat you as.'

Translated 'the matter' — taking ⲡⲉⲁⲡ as a Lyc. variant on the ⲱⲡ/ⲍⲉⲡ family of nouns ('reckoning, judgment, matter'), introducing the topic-clause that follows ('that you may see no sins...'). Could alternatively be 'the judgment' or 'the reckoning'; chose 'matter' as most idiomatic in the conditional-purpose context.

Translated 'do not at all despise' — taking ⲛⲧⲁϩ as an emphatic intensifier (cf. Sah. ⲛ̄ⲧⲟϥ 'indeed') reinforcing the prohibition. Alternative parsing as causative-conjunctive 'let yourself' is possible but less natural.

Translated 'they being firm of heart' — ⲛⲁⲃⲥ tentatively read as a Lyc. qualitative meaning 'be firm/at peace,' fitting the contrast with ⲙⲛⲧⲧⲱⲛ 'contention' in lines 13-14. Lexeme not securely attested; awaiting parallels.

Translated 'the moment in which a contention shall arise' — ⲙⲛⲧⲧⲱⲛ 'contention' (in glossary) as the cosmic-affective event among the holy when the indwelling Old Man stirs them. The catechumen now grasps Mani's earlier teaching that conflict among saints is not their own action but the Old Man within them.
Translated 'they habitually receive injury' — ⲉⲡⲏⲣⲓⲁ from Greek ἐπήρεια 'insult, injury, abusive treatment.' The holy ones suffer mutual injury because of the dwelling of the Old Man in their flesh.

Translated 'they are stirred up' — taking ⲥⲉⲗⲉⲃⲗⲉⲃ as a Lyc. reduplicated verbal form denoting agitated mutual disturbance, in keeping with the iterative-affective pattern of pairs like ⲥⲱⲣϣⲣ̄ 'scatter' or ϫⲱϩⲙ̄ 'defile.' Could also render 'quarrel' or 'agitate one another.' Etymology uncertain.
Translated 'I shall ask you a saying' — ϣⲛⲧ Lyc. for ϣⲓⲛⲉ 'inquire'; the cognate-object construction ϣⲓⲛⲉ + ⲥⲉⲭⲉ makes 'ask a word/saying' rather than just 'ask a question.'

Translated 'Now then, give attention!' — ⲧⲱⲉⲧⲱ is unattested elsewhere; functions here as an attention-getting interjection introducing the corrective ϯ-ⲍⲧⲏⲕ 'set/give your heart.' Could also be a Lycopolitan reflex of an imperative meaning 'attend!' or a Greek loan (e.g., τοίνυν 'therefore'). Translated functionally.

Translated as the question-formula 'truly, or no?' — ϩⲁⲛⲓⲧ taken as 'truly/sincerely' (function-equivalent to ⲟⲛⲧⲱⲥ or ϩⲁⲡⲗⲱⲥ); ⲭⲛ̄ ⲙⲙⲁⲛ as standard Coptic 'or not'; ϩⲍⲁⲩ as a closing question-particle (possibly 'in any wise'). The whole functions as a yes/no challenge.

Parsed ⲁⲩ- as the perfect prefix on indefinite ⲟⲩ-ⲛⲁⲍⲟⲣⲉⲩⲥ 'a Nazoraean,' yielding 'a Nazoraean came up.' ⲙⲡⲙⲏⲧ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ⲙ̄- as the spatial idiom 'in the midst before/in front of' = 'in the presence of the Apostle.'

The chapter heading is split across lines 19-20 by the Coptic word-break in ⲛⲁⲍⲟ-|ⲣⲉⲩⲥ. Translated each line preserving the visual layout, with English 'Naz-' / 'oraean.' The chapter number ⲡⲑ (89) frames the heading on line 20.

Translated 'fight together with us for the Land of Light' — taking ⲁ- as the directional 'for/towards' rather than adversative 'against,' since the Land of Light is the cosmic homeland the elect contend for, not against. The yokefellow image confirms a common combatant standing with the brothers.
